## Natural history notes

A tough, leathery wood-decay mushroom characterized by a tan to brown, often hairy or fringed cap and saw-toothed gill edges that give it the “sawgill” appearance. In Florida, the Fringed Sawgill grows on dead hardwood logs, branches, stumps, and woody debris in hammocks, hardwood forests, mixed woods, parks, and shaded yards. It functions as a decomposer, breaking down dead wood and helping recycle nutrients while providing habitat and food for small insects and other forest-floor organisms.
